items.text: New Zealand officials fined a 50-year-old man for attempting to ‘body slam’ an orca near Devonport, Auckland. The incident was recorded on video and posted on Instagram. It showed the man deliberately trying to touch the orca while others on the boat laughed and cheered. The Department of Conservation called his actions reckless and dangerous for both himself and the male orca, which was swimming with a calf. Investigation officers expressed shock at the man’s behavior and highlighted the potential risk to both the man and the orca. Orcas, also known as killer whales, are the largest member of the dolphin family and are critically endangered in New Zealand, with fewer than 200 left. The man’s actions were illegal, as disturbing or swimming with marine mammals is prohibited. The man was fined 600 dollars, and fortunately, the orcas involved were not significantly harmed. Difficult words: reckless (careless and without thought of the consequences), potential (possible), endangered (at risk of dying out). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A video on social media showed a man jumping off a boat and touching an orca. Other people in the video laughed and cheered. The incident happened near Devonport, Auckland, when a male orca and a calf were swimming near the boat. Orcas are very important in New Zealand and are at high risk of extinction . There are fewer than 200 animals left. It is illegal to disturb or swim with them. New Zealand fined the 50-year-old man 600 dollars for trying to touch the animal. Officials said the man’s actions were very dangerous for both himself and the orca. Luckily, the animals didn’t get hurt. Difficult words: calf (a young animal, for example, a cow, elephant, or whale), extinction (when an animal no longer exists), disturb (to make someone scared or worried). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man in New Zealand must pay 600 dollars. He jumps off a boat. He touches an orca. There is a video of this incident on social media. Other people are on the boat. A male orca and a baby orca are swimming nearby. The people laugh and cheer when the man jumps in the water. The incident happens near Devonport, Auckland. The man is 50 years old. There are only a few orcas in New Zealand. People must protect them. It is against the law to touch the animals or swim with them. Authorities say that it is also dangerous for both people and the animals. It is a stupid thing to do. Difficult words: cheer (to be happy and shout), protect (to keep safe), law (rules of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi died in a helicopter crash near the Azerbaijan border. The crash was caused by poor weather, and it also killed Foreign Minister Hossein Amirabdollahian and six others. Supreme Leader Khamenei declared five days of public mourning and announced that First Vice President Mohammad Mokhber would serve as interim president. Raisi’s death occurred during a time of political and social unrest in Iran, with international pressure over its nuclear program and ties with Russia. The public reaction to Raisi’s death was mixed. Government supporters gathered to mourn, while others, particularly those opposing Raisi’s policies, expressed muted reactions or even celebrated his death. This reflects the deep divisions in Iranian society over the clerical regime’s handling of various crises. Difficult words: interim (temporary), unrest (disagreements or fighting between groups of people), clerical (related to the formal church-based leadership). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi died in a helicopter crash near the Azerbaijan border. The crash also killed Foreign Minister Hossein Amirabdollahian and six others. The bad weather caused the crash. Officials announced five days of mourning and said that the First Vice President Mohammad Mokhber will be the temporary president. Raisi’s death comes at a time when Iran is facing many problems, like its nuclear program and contacts with Russia. People in Iran had different reactions to his death. Some mourned him, but others who were against his strict policies were not sad and even celebrated. This shows that people in Iran have different opinions about the government’s actions. Difficult words: mourning (a time of sadness after someone dies), temporary (lasting only for some time), policy (ideas or a plan of a business, government, or group of people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi dies in a helicopter crash. The accident happens near the Azerbaijan border . The weather is bad. Six other people also die. One of them is the Foreign Minister. There are five days of mourning in the country. Mohammad Mokhber will be the new president for now. Some people in Iran are sad about Raisi’s death. But others are not. Some people are even happy about it. This situation shows that people in Iran have different ideas about the government. The country has many problems. People fight and protest. Some countries are not happy about Iran’s nuclear program and contacts with Russia. Difficult words: border (a line between two countries), mourning (the time when people are sad after someone dies), nuclear program (getting materials, making and testing a nuclear bomb). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A plane traveling from London to Singapore experienced severe turbulence and was forced to an emergency landing at Bangkok Airport. One passenger, a 73-year-old British man, likely died from a heart attack. Additionally, 30 people were injured, including seven critically. The Boeing 777 hit an air pocket in Thai airspace, which led to turbulence. Many passengers and crew members were treated at a field hospital on the tarmac . One passenger recounted the terrifying moment when the turbulence hit. He described how objects flew through the air, and some passengers were injured. The seatbelt sign had just turned on when the turbulence occurred. The man was uninjured because he had fastened his seatbelt in time. Airline experts noted that sudden turbulence with no warning is rare but possible. The incident resulted in one death, seven critical injuries, and multiple other injuries among passengers and crew. Difficult words: turbulence (violent and unsteady movement of air), air pocket (an area in the sky where the air is flowing differently from the way it is in the surroundings), tarmac (a material used for surfacing roads or other outdoor areas). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A plane was flying from London to Singapore but it had to land in Bangkok because of strong turbulence . The Boeing 777 hit an air pocket in Thai airspace. An air pocket is an area where the air is flowing differently. One 73-year-old British man died, probably from a heart attack. Thirty people were hurt, and seven were in serious condition . Many passengers got treatment at the airport, immediately after the landing. One passenger said that the turbulence was very strong. He saw objects flying and people getting hurt. He fastened his seatbelt just in time but some people didn’t. Experts say that such strong turbulence is rare but sometimes it can happen. Difficult words: turbulence (a strong movement of air), condition (how someone or something is or feels), treatment (how someone deals with someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A plane is flying from London to Singapore. There are problems. The plane flies through strong turbulence . The Boeing 777 hits an air pocket, an area where the air moves differently. Thirty people are hurt, seven very badly. One man dies. He probably gets a heart attack . He is 73 years old. He is British. Andrew Davies is one of the passengers . He says that the plane moves a lot. Things are flying around. Andrew fastens his seatbelt. Not all people have enough time to do it. The plane must land in Bangkok. Emergency workers are ready at the airport. Such strong turbulence does not happen often. But it can happen. Difficult words: turbulence (when air moves a lot), heart attack (when your heart stops), passenger (a person who travels by plane, bus, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dozens of red fire ant nests have been found in Sicily, Italy. These aggressive ants from South America, also known as Solenopsis invicta, are a feared invasive species. The ants can damage plants by eating their roots, and they attack helpful insects. The EU considers these ants a serious threat. They were first noticed in Europe last year, and now scientists are working to control them. Countries like Brazil, China, and the US spend billions trying to manage these ants; however, they still cause significant damage. The ants probably arrived in Sicily from Brazil, but the exact details are unknown. So far, there hasn’t been major damage, but if the ants spread, agriculture and fruit production could suffer. The ants thrive in places with water, like gardens and playgrounds. The Sicilian government is taking action, appointing foresters to handle the situation. They use steam machines to destroy ant nests. The goal is to kill the queens to stop the colonies. Difficult words: invasive (spreading harmfully), thrive (grow well), forester (a person in charge of a forest, or skilled in planting, managing, or caring for trees). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last year, scientists saw red fire ants in Europe for the first time. Now, they found red fire ant nests in Sicily, Italy. These ants come from South America and are very dangerous and aggressive . They can damage plants and attack helpful insects . The EU considers these ants a serious problem. The ants probably came to Sicily from Brazil, but no one knows how. Countries like Brazil, China, and the US spend a lot of money trying to control these ants, but they still cause a lot of damage. So far, there is not much damage in Italy, but there are still more nests. The Sicilian government is working to kill the ants. Workers use steam machines which destroy ant nests. The idea is to kill the queens. Difficult words: nest (a place where birds or other animals lay eggs and keep their young), aggressive (ready to attack), insect (a small animal with wigs and six legs). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists find dangerous red ants in Sicily, Italy. They first see these ants in Europe last year. These ants come from South America. They are a big problem in Brazil, China, and the US. These countries spend a lot of money on killing the ants. These ants hurt plants. They eat the roots . They attack other insects. Nobody knows how these ants get to Europe. But they can be a big problem for Europe in the future. They often are in gardens and playgrounds. In Sicily, workers use steam machines. They destroy ants. But there are still new nests. It is necessary to kill the queens. Difficult words: ant (a small insect with a sting), root (the part of a plant which is under the ground), steam (when water boils and turns into hot gas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Political violence is rising in the European Union because of extremism and disappointment with the government. The recent shooting of Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico highlights this rise. This was the first attack on a European head of state since 2003. Analysts from the European Policy Centre say the political climate and upcoming elections are partly to blame. Extreme political groups are becoming stronger, which leads to more verbal and physical violence and a polarized society. In Germany, attacks on politicians have nearly doubled in the last five years, with 2,790 incidents in 2023. France also saw a 32% increase in attacks on politicians in 2022. Experts say that people don’t trust authorities and feel vulnerable . They warn that this environment may discourage people from getting involved in politics. Difficult words: extremism (having strong political or religious views), polarized (divided into two opposing groups), vulnerable (open to harm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Political violence is growing in the European Union. Many people are starting to have strong political views, and they are feeling unhappy with the government. Recently, a man shot Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico. This was the first attack on a European leader since 2003. Experts say that the political climate and elections are part of the problem. Extreme political groups are getting stronger, which leads to more violence. In Germany, attacks on politicians almost doubled in five years, with 2,790 incidents in 2023. France also saw more attacks on politicians, with a 32% increase in 2022. People don’t trust the government and feel weak, which can stop them from joining politics. Difficult words: violence (actions which hurt other people), political climate (people’s mood about politics), extreme (having very strong views and ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More and more people in the EU are not happy with the politics. Political violence is growing. There are more attacks on politicians. More people are having extreme ideas. Recently, a man shoots Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico. This is the first attack on a European leader since 2003. There are more problems, the elections and the political mood of people. Extreme political groups are getting stronger across Europe. It brings more violence. In Germany, attacks on politicians almost double in five years. There are 2,790 attacks in 2023. In France, there are 32% more attacks on politicians in 2022. People do not believe that politicians are doing good things for them. They do not want to be in politics anymore. Difficult words: violence (hurting others), extreme (strong and unusual), elections (when people vote people for a job in politics). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Italy has the oldest population in the European Union, and one in four people are over 65. The country is home to the world’s fastest 90-year-old woman sprinter, Emma Maria Mazzenga. Born on August 1, 1933, Mazzenga recently set a new world record in the 90 and over age group by running 200 meters in 51.47 seconds. She holds five world records, nine European records, and 28 Italian records in Masters sprinting. Masters sprinting is competitive racing for older athletes. Mazzenga expressed her surprise and happiness at her latest achievement . Despite often having no direct rivals in her age category, she focuses on achieving good times. Mazzenga started running again at 53 after a long break and finds great comfort and community in her athletic career. She plans to compete in the Italian championships in June and hopes to attend the world championships in Sweden next year, though she jokes about not making long-term plans. Difficult words: achievement (things done successfully with effort), rival (a person or group competing with others). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Italy has the oldest population in the European Union. One in four people is over 65 years old. It is no surprise that Italy has the world’s fastest 90-year-old woman sprinter, Emma Maria Mazzenga. Mazzenga was born on August 1, 1933. She set a new world record by running 200 meters in 51.47 seconds. She holds five world records and many European and Italian records in Masters sprinting, which is for older runners. Mazzenga was happy and surprised by her latest record. She often runs without rivals in her age group and focuses on getting good times. Mazzenga started running again at 53 and finds it comforting and social. She will compete in the Italian championships in June and hopes to take part in the world championships in Sweden next year. But she jokes about not making many plans. Difficult words: rival (a person or group who competes with others), focus (to give special attention to something), comforting (making you feel less sad or worried). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Italy has many old people. One in four people are over 65 years old. Emma Maria Mazzenga is 90 years old. She is the fastest runner in her age group. She is born on August 1, 1933. She runs 200 meters in 51.47 seconds. It is a new world record . She has five world records and many European and Italian records. Mazzenga is happy and surprised about her new record. She often has no other runners in her age group. She tries to get good times. Mazzenga starts running again at 53 years old. Running makes her happy. She meets many people. She will run in the Italian championships in June. She hopes to go to the world championships in Sweden next year. But she jokes about not making many plans. Difficult words: record (the best result), surprised (when you cannot believe something), joke (to say funny things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists may have solved the mystery of how Egypt’s 31 pyramids, including the famous Giza complex, were built over 4,000 years ago. Researchers from the University of North Carolina Wilmington discovered that the pyramids were likely constructed along an ancient, now-hidden part of the River Nile. Previously, archaeologists thought that Egyptians used a nearby river to transport materials like stone blocks to build the pyramids. However, the exact location and nature of this waterway were unknown until now. The dried-up branch of the Nile shows that materials could be moved year-round, not just during the flood season. This discovery helps us understand the logistics of pyramid building and suggests that ancient Egypt’s landscape was different from what we believed. The area around the pyramids was likely more accessible due to river routes, which explains why pyramids were built in clusters . Future studies will look at how this changes our understanding of ancient Egypt’s topography . Difficult words: logistics (the detailed organization of resources), cluster (a group of similar things that occur together), topography (the arrangement of physical features of an area). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists believe that they found out how people built Egypt’s pyramids over 4,000 years ago. A team from the University of North Carolina Wilmington found an old part of the River Nile which is now dry. Before, people thought the Egyptians used a river to move big stone blocks and other materials to build the pyramids. But no one knew where the river was until now. This dry part of the Nile shows that people could move stones all year, not only during the flood season . This new idea helps us understand more about how the building happened. It also shows that Egypt was very different from what we believed. Nowadays, we know that pyramids are in clusters because they are near this river. Future studies will tell us more about how Egypt looked in the past. Difficult words: flood season (time of the year when a large amount of water covers an area which is usually dry), cluster (a group of similar things which are close together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists know better how people build Egypt’s pyramids over 4,000 years ago. A team from the University of North Carolina finds an old part of the River Nile. It is now dry . We believe that Egyptians move big stones on the river. They use the stones to build the pyramids. But scientists do not know where the river is, until now. This dry river shows that people can move the stones all year. Now, we understand more about how the building happens. We also know that Egypt looks different in the past. Pyramids are in groups because they are near the river. In the future, we will learn more about what Egypt looks like in the past. Difficult words: pyramid (an old stone structure in Egypt and other countries), dry (not wet), future (time which will come). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Slovakian Prime Minister Robert Fico was shot in the town of Handlová, approximately 145km from the capital, Bratislava. The incident, which was captured on video by broadcaster RTV Prievidza, shows Fico being shot by a man in the crowd. The shooter fired five shots, hitting Fico, who then fell to the ground before security personnel subdued the attacker. Fico was airlifted to Banská Bystrica and is in a life-threatening condition, according to officials. The shooting happened outside the House of Culture in Handlová following a Slovak government meeting. The suspect has been detained by the police. Difficult words: subdue (to restrain), airlift (to move supplies or people by aircraft, especially in a difficult or dangerous situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was an attack on Slovakian Prime Minister Robert Fico in the town of Handlová, about 145 kilometers from the capital, Bratislava. A video showed Fico being shot by a man in the crowd . The man fired five times. Fico fell to the ground, and security personnel quickly caught the shooter. Emergency services transported Fico to Banská Bystrica for treatment, and he is in a life-threatening condition . The shooting happened outside the House of Culture in Handlová after a government meeting. The police arrested the suspect . Difficult words: crowd (a large number of people in one place), life-threatening condition (an illness or injury due to which a person may die), suspect (a person who the police believe did something wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is an attack on Slovakian Prime Minister Robert Fico. A man shoots Fico. The attack happens in Handlová, a town which is 145 kilometers from Bratislava, the capital city. A video shows how the man shoots Fico. The man fires five times. Fico falls. Police catch the shooter. Fico is in hospital in Banská Bystrica. The situation is serious . The shooting happens outside the House of Culture in Handlová after a politicians meeting. Difficult words: fire (to use a gun to shoot), serious (hard or complicated). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

OpenAI has introduced the latest version of the technology behind its AI chatbot ChatGPT, called GPT-4o. This new version will be available to all ChatGPT users, including non-subscribers. It is faster and designed to sound chatty and sometimes flirtatious . GPT-4o can read and discuss images, translate languages, and recognize emotions from facial expressions. This launch marks a significant step in the race for dominance in generative AI, with OpenAI leading the way. The new chatbot can interact via voice, helping with tasks like preparing for presentations and solving math problems. OpenAI’s advancements come ahead of expected announcements from competitors like Google, Microsoft, and Apple. Difficult words: flirtatious (expressing a playful sexual attraction), dominance (a leading position), advancement (a development or improvement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

OpenAI just launched a new version of its AI chatbot called GPT-4o. This version will be available to everyone who uses ChatGPT, even those who don’t pay. It is faster and can sound more conversational and sometimes even playful. GPT-4o can also look at and talk about pictures, translate languages, and understand emotions from faces. The new chatbot can talk back to you and help with things like preparing for presentations and solving math problems. This is a big step in the competition for AI technology, and OpenAI is the leader now. Other big tech companies like Google, Microsoft, and Apple will probably come with similar news soon. Difficult words: available (when people can use or get something), conversational (when someone can take part in a talk), competition (when a person or company is trying to be better than others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

OpenAI has a new AI chatbot . It is called GPT-4o. Everyone can use ChatGPT. You can use it for free. The new GPT-4o is faster. It talks in a friendly way. GPT-4o can look at pictures, translate languages, and understand feelings from faces. This is a big thing in the AI world. Company OpenAI is the leader in the AI world now. The new chatbot can talk to you. It can help with presentations . Also, it can solve math problems. Other big companies like Google, Microsoft, and Apple will come with something similar soon. Difficult words: chatbot (a computer program which speaks to you like a real person), translate (to change words into a different language), presentation (a talk about a new product or idea). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Kharkiv, Ukraine, a new underground school has opened to protect children from Russian attacks. Hundreds of students began their classes this week in the bunker school, located 6 meters underground. The entrance is through a small white concrete box on the pavement, and the windowless classrooms are brightly lit and painted in white and lime green. Kharkiv lies near the Russian border and has faced relentless attacks since the beginning of the invasion 26 months ago. The increased airstrikes and fighting have made the new school a necessity. Masha, 9, and her brother Oleksii, 6, were excited to attend in-person classes and meet their teachers and friends. Their mother, Marina Prikhodko, expressed her joy at seeing her children excited for school. The school’s enrollment is 300 students, and it will expand to 900 by September. City’s Mayor hopes this initiative will normalize life amidst ongoing conflict. Difficult words: relentless (never stopping), enrollment (registering at an institution), initiative (a new plan or action). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new school in Kharkiv, Ukraine, is underground to keep children safe from Russian attacks. Many students started classes this week in the bunker , 6 meters below the ground. The entrance is a small white concrete box, and the classrooms are bright but have no windows. Kharkiv is close to the Russian border. Russia attacked it several times since the war started 26 months ago. The underground school is important because children can see their teachers and friends. The school has 300 students now and will have 900 by September. Mayor Ihor Terekhov wants this school to help children live normal lives. Many children wore traditional Ukrainian shirts for the opening day. Difficult words: bunker (a place where people can hide), entrance (an opening which allows you to get to a place), traditional (usual, typical). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new school opens in Kharkiv, Ukraine. The school is underground. It keeps children safe. It’s the first underground school in Ukraine. The school is important for children. They do not need to have online classes. They can meet with their teachers and friends. And they are safe. The school is 6 meters under the ground. The entrance is a small white box. The classrooms are bright. But they have no windows. Kharkiv is near Russia. Russia attacks the city many times. The school has 300 students now. It will have 900 students in September. The Mayor says that this school helps children live normal lives. Many children wear traditional Ukrainian shirts on the first day. Difficult words: entrance (an opening through which you get to a place), normal (usual), traditional (typical). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Switzerland won the Eurovision Song Contest, with Nemo, the first nonbinary contestant, claiming the crystal microphone. Their song ‘The Code’ blends various genres like drum-and-bass, opera, rap, and rock, and it narrates Nemo’s journey of self-discovery as a nonbinary person. Despite protests against Israel’s actions in Gaza, Switzerland’s victory stood out. Nemo expressed pride, highlighted the importance of queer representation in Eurovision and the impact of their song on others. Dutch journalist Frank van Dijk praised Switzerland’s win as deserved and highlighted the contest’s shift toward rewarding quality songs and staging. Additionally, the disqualification of Dutch singer Yus Klein before the final sparked anger, and many deemed it disproportionate . Difficult words: nonbinary (not identifying exclusively as a male or female), blend (to mix different things or substances), disproportionate (not in proper relation or balance). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Switzerland won a big singing contest called Eurovision. Nemo became the first nonbinary singer to win the contest. They won with their song ‘The Code’. This song mixes different kinds of music and talks about Nemo’s story of finding out who they are. Although there were protests against Israel’s attack on Gaza during the contest, when Switzerland won Nemo was proud . They said that it was important for people like them to be in the contest. A Dutch journalist said that Switzerland deserved to win. But people were upset because a singer from the Netherlands got kicked out of the contest before it finished. Difficult words: contest (an event in which people compete with each other), nonbinary (when a person does not say if they are a man or woman), proud (pleased). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Eurovision is a big singing contest . Singers from European countries compete. This year, Switzerland wins. Nemo is the winner. This singer is nonbinary. The singer does not say if they are a boy or a girl. They with their song ‘The Code’. Nemo is proud . They are the first nonbinary winner ever. Nemo says that people like them must be in the contest. A journalist from the Netherlands says that Switzerland deserves to win. People were protesting against Israel’s army in Gaza during the contest. People are also upset because a singer from the Netherlands must leave the contest before it ends. Difficult words: contest (an event in which people compete with each other), proud (pleased), deserve (to get something because of good work). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brazilian athletes, originally from Rio Grande do Sul, are sacrificing their Olympic dreams to help flood victims. Rowers Evaldo Becker and Piedro Tuchtenhagen, set to compete, decided to assist in rescue efforts. Swimmer Viviane Jungblut, who had already qualified for the Olympics, withdrew to focus on recovery operations. World surfing champion Italo Ferreira and Brazil’s judo team coach, Antonio Carlos Kiko Pereira, also joined rescue work. Despite plans to relocate athletes for training, many stayed to help. Former Olympic athletes, including gymnast Daiane dos Santos and swimmer Nicholas Santos, volunteered. The floods in Rio Grande do Sul have caused significant casualties and displacement . Although water levels dropped temporarily, more rain is expected, raising concerns for further flooding. Difficult words: sacrifice (to give up something valued to help another person), displacement (the situation in which people are forced to leave the place where they normally live). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Brazilian athletes in Rio Grande do Sul are helping flood victims instead of following their Olympic dreams. Rowers Evaldo Becker and Piedro Tuchtenhagen decided to help in rescue efforts. Swimmer Viviane Jungblut withdrew from the Olympics to focus on helping. World surfing champion Italo Ferreira and Brazil’s judo team coach, Antonio Carlos Kiko Pereira, also joined rescue work. There were plans to relocate athletes for training, but many stayed to help. Former Olympic athletes, for example, gymnast Daiane dos Santos and swimmer Nicholas Santos, volunteered . The floods in Rio Grande do Sul killed many people and forced thousands to leave their homes. Water levels dropped, but people expect more rain to come. Difficult words: withdraw (to decide not to take part), relocate (to move from one place to another), volunteer (to freely offer to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brazilian athletes from Rio Grande do Sul are helping people after big floods . Rowers Evaldo Becker and Piedro Tuchtenhagen help rescue people. Swimmer Viviane Jungblut also wants to help. She says that she will not take part in the Olympics. World surfing champion Italo Ferreira and Brazil’s judo team coach, Antonio Carlos Kiko Pereira, are helping too. Athletes can move away and get ready for the Olympics somewhere else. But many stay and help. Former Olympic athletes, like gymnast Daiane dos Santos and swimmer Nicholas Santos, are helping too. The floods in Rio Grande do Sul hurt many people. More rain is coming. There may be more floods. Difficult words: floods (when there is too much water in rivers), rescue (to save someone), former (happening in an earlier time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Apple recently issued an apology following negative feedback about an advert. The one-minute commercial depicted the destruction of various creative tools by a hydraulic press. The video was meant to demonstrate how creativity had been compressed into the latest iPad; however, it received criticism for not empowering creatives as intended. Celebrities like Hugh Grant and Justine Bateman expressed shock at the destruction depicted. Apple’s marketing boss acknowledged the misstep and expressed regret. The company’s CEO, Tim Cook, faced criticism for a related social media post. Despite aiming to highlight the new tablet’s features, the ad was seen as potentially hindering creativity. Critics worried about the impact of technology on artistic expression. Difficult words: creative (an informal word for a person whose job involves creative work), misstep (a mistake or error), hinder (to cause delay or difficulty). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Apple said sorry for their latest iPad advert . The one-minute video showed a hydraulic press breaking things. The video wanted to highlight what the new iPad could do, but people didn’t like it. They were upset by it. They thought technologies might take over and stop people from being creative. Even famous people criticized the advert on social media. Apple’s marketing boss said sorry, and he said that the advert was a mistake. The company’s boss was criticized for his social media post about the advert. Some people in Japan didn’t like it either. They said that it was bad to break things. Difficult words: advert (a video about a product or service), hydraulic press (a machine which presses things), highlight (to point out). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Apple has a new advert . The video is one minute long. It is about the new iPad. But people do not like it. A hydraulic press breaks things in the video. The video wants to show what the new iPad can do. But people are upset. Even some famous people say that the video is bad. People think that things like iPad will stop creativity . They worry that these things will take over. People in Japan do not like the advert. They say that it is very bad to break things. Apple’s marketing boss says sorry. He says that the advert is a mistake. People are also angry at the social media post by Apple’s boss Tim Cook. Difficult words: advert (a short video about a product or service), hydraulic press (a machine which presses things), creativity (having new and unusual ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

National elections are taking place in India, the world’s largest democracy. The country holds the vote in phases across several weeks to allow the country’s nearly one billion voters to participate. A total of seven phases will be completed by June 1st. A pressing issue in this election is youth unemployment. It is a growing problem as half of India’s 1.4 billion people are under the age of 30. Prime Minister Narendra Modi pledged millions of jobs when he first came to power in 2014; however, during the last decade, he has largely failed to deliver. Now, as he tries to lead the ruling BJP party to a rare third term, the question is: do voters trust him to address this challenge? Difficult words: pressing (requiring quick or immediate action or attention), pledge (to promise). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

India, the world’s biggest democracy, is currently holding national elections. There are several phases over weeks so that nearly one billion voters can take part. Last week, millions were voting in the third phase across 95 areas. All seven phases will end on June 1st. Youth unemployment is a big problem. Half of India’s 1.4 billion population is under 30, and finding a job is getting more and more difficult for them. India’s Prime Minister got to power in 2014. He promised millions of jobs but failed. He would like to win the elections again, but the question for millions of Indians is if he can deal with the problem this time. Difficult words: phase (a stage in a series of events or a process), youth (young people), unemployment (a situation in which someone doesn’t have a job). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

India is the world’s biggest democracy . There are elections now. Indians vote to choose people for jobs in politics. The elections are in different parts. There are too many people. All people must have a chance to vote. There are seven parts altogether . The elections end on June 1st. A big problem is that many young people do not have jobs. India has 1.4 billion people. Half of them are under 30 years old. The Prime Minister is in power since 2014. He says that he will get new jobs. But it does not happen. He wants to be the boss for the third time. But will Indians believe him again? Difficult words: democracy (the system when people of a country vote to choose leaders), altogether (completely, in total), Prime Minister (the leader of a government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Wednesday, the EU countries started negotiations on the next round of sanctions against Russia, which targets LNG, liquefied natural gas, for the first time. The proposal aims to stop the practice of trans-shipment , where LNG received at EU ports is sent to other countries. Additionally, the sanctions target three Russian LNG projects not yet operational . However, the Russian government has been effectively finding ways around previous restrictions in the oil sector, which brings doubts about how effective the proposed measures will be. Despite initial discussions, reaching a final agreement among the 27 member states may take weeks due to the sensitivity of energy sector sanctions. Difficult words: liquefied (made liquid), trans-shipment (the process of transferring goods from one ship to another), operational (working or ready for use). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

European countries are discussing new rules to stop the movement of Russian natural gas. The EU wants to prevent Russian gas from being sent to other countries after arriving in European ports. With these rules, the EU wants to put Russia under pressure and hurt its economy. So far, the Russian government always found ways to deal with sanctions . That is why some people doubt if the new rules will help. It is not easy to make a deal among all twenty-seven member countries. Therefore, to agree on the new rules may take some time. Difficult words: prevent (to stop something from happening), pressure (force or influence), sanction (an action which a country or countries take to force a country to follow international laws). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

EU countries want to stop Russia from selling natural gas to other places. It is happening now. When the gas gets to Europe, other ships take it to many countries. Russia makes a lot of money by selling gas. This gas passes through Europe. This idea is to make Russia weaker in the gas market . But Russia is clever. They find ways of dealing with similar rules in the past. This fact worries people. They are not sure if these new rules will work. Twenty-seven countries are in the EU. It takes time to talk about the rules. They need time to decide what to do next. Difficult words: pass through (to make a journey from one place to another), gas market (buying and selling gas), deal (to solve a situation or problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel has ordered a ban on Al Jazeera, stopping the Qatari news network’s broadcasts in the country and access to its website. The decision was made by Benjamin Netanyahu’s cabinet, and officials cited concerns over national security and alleged Al Jazeera’s alignment with Hamas. Al Jazeera strongly criticized the move, labeled it a dangerous decision, and promised to take legal action. Walid Omary, the network’s bureau chief in the occupied West Bank, emphasized the intention to obstruct coverage of the conflict in Gaza, Israel, and the West Bank. This latest development underscores the ongoing tensions between Israel and Al Jazeera. Previously, the network accused Israel of targeting its facilities and personnel. Difficult words: alignment (association or collaboration), coverage (the reporting of a particularly important event or subject), underscore (to emphasize the importance of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Benjamin Netanyahu’s cabinet decided to ban Al Jazeera, the Qatari news network. Israeli people will not have access to its website and will not be able to watch broadcasts . Officials said that Al Jazeera supported Hamas and it was dangerous for the country’s security . Al Jazeera argued that this was not true, and they plan to take legal action. According to Al Jazeera’s boss, the government wants to hide information about the situation in Gaza. The ban follows long-running problems between Israel and Al Jazeera. In the past, Al Jazeera said that Israel attacked its people and buildings. Difficult words: broadcast (to transmit a program or some information by radio or television), security (being safe), hide (to keep secret or away from people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Benjamin Netanyahu is the leader of the Israeli government. His people ban Al Jazeera. Al Jazeera is a Qatari news network. They have problems with Israel in the past. Now, people in Israel will not access Al Jazeera’s website. They will not be able to watch the news. Al Jazeera says that Israel wants to keep important information away from people. Al Jazeera plans legal action . This is one of many problems between Israel and Al Jazeera. Al Jazeera says that Israel attacks their people and buildings, too. Difficult words: ban (to officially stop), access (being able to get somewhere), legal action (when someone asks a court for help). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Residents in central Gaza face a critical issue as domestic waste accumulates near their homes. Within a mere 150 meters, a makeshift landfill poses serious health risks and raises concerns about children’s well-being. Since the beginning of the conflict between Israel and Hamas, municipal services in Gaza haven’t been effective due to road blockages. Local people turn to alternative dumping sites that are not designated dumping zones. Domestic waste is piling up which leads to environmental degradation. Some people confirm the emergence of unprecedented diseases like sore skin and fevers, which, they believe, is a consequence of the waste’s toxicity. Officials warn that the waste could attract insects and stray animals and potentially contaminate the groundwater. International assistance is necessary to mitigat e these environmental and health hazards. Difficult words: makeshift (temporary), unprecedented (never done or seen before), mitigate (to make something less severe or harmful). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

When the conflict between Israel and Hamas started, authorities blocked some roads. As a result, trucks which collect people’s waste can’t get to dumping sites . People throw away a lot of things and they are looking for places where to put their waste. Alternative dumping sites appear just hundreds of meters from their homes. Waste is piling up and some people are getting worried about their children’s health. Doctors report unusual skin problems and fevers, which they associate with the waste. Officials say that the waste could contaminate water and international help may be necessary. Difficult words: block (to make a road, pipe, or a place impossible to go through), dumping site (a place where people throw away waste), contaminate (to make something less pure or make it toxic). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in Gaza have a problem with waste near their homes. When the conflict between Israel and Hamas starts, people cannot use some roads. Big vehicles get people’s waste to a special place called a dumping site. Now, the trucks cannot get to the site. But there is more and more waste. People do not know what to do. They throw away waste at several places in the town. These places are dangerous. Children have skin problems and fevers . They do not have these problems before. Officials say that these places are toxic . They can make water dirty. Gaza needs help from other countries. Difficult words: waste (things and materials which people throw away), fever (a high body temperature), toxic (dangerous for people and their health). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Czech Republic marked 20 years of being part of the European Union with a big event at Prague Castle. They celebrated their membership anniversary with famous people in attendance. The Czech Prime Minister talked about supporting other countries like Ukraine to join the EU if they meet the requirements. He stressed the importance of being transparent and fair in this process. The Czech President highlighted that EU and NATO memberships were important for the country’s freedom, prosperity , and security. German President Steinmeier emphasized that Europe should stand together against threats and consider Ukraine as part of Europe. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy expressed his hope that Ukraine would join the EU soon and thanked the Czech Republic for its support. Difficult words: transparent (honest), highlight (to emphasize something important), prosperity (the conditions of being successful or thriving). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Czech Republic became a member of the EU 20 years ago. European leaders and other famous people celebrated this event at Prague Castle. The Czech Prime Minister said that more countries should join the EU, for example Ukraine. But they need to follow the rules. It is necessary to be fair and transparent about this. The Czech President said that EU and NATO membership is very important for their country’s freedom and safety. The German President said that Europe should stay together and think of Ukraine as part of Europe. The Ukrainian President hoped that Ukraine could join the EU soon and thanked the Czech Republic for its help in the war with Russia. Difficult words: transparent (honest), membership (being a member), freedom (when you are free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a big party at Prague Castle. 20 years ago, the Czech Republic becomes a member of the EU. The Prime Minister says that more countries should be in the EU, for example Ukraine. But these countries must follow rules. They must be fair and honest . The Czech President speaks at the party, too. He says that it is good for the country to be in the EU and NATO. The country is free and safe. Other leaders want Europe to stay together. They say that Ukraine is part of Europe. The Ukrainian President hopes that Ukraine can join the EU soon. He thanks the Czech Republic for helping in the war with Russia. Difficult words: member (a person or country which belongs to a group of other people or countries), honest (open), join (to become part of a group of people or things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dublin took strong action to remove a tent city housing migrants and refugees. The city employed a large convoy of police vehicles, council trucks, and coaches. The camp of about 200 tents was situated near the government’s International Protection Office. It had grown too large and visible and drew attention to Ireland’s problems with migration. According to authorities, the removal was necessary due to safety and hygiene reasons; however, it sparked controversy due to its timing and political implications. Just days earlier, tensions had escalated between Ireland and the UK over migration. Both governments are facing pressure to control the influx of migrants. Removing the tent city raised questions about the treatment of asylum seekers and the effectiveness of migration policies. Critics labeled it as a form of cleansing, and they emphasized the need for dignified solutions to deal with migration challenges. Difficult words: controversy (public disagreement or heated discussion), influx (an arrival or entry of large numbers of people or things), dignified (deserving respect or serious and calm manner). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Dublin cleaned up a tent city in the city center. Migrants and refugees lived in about 200 tents near the International Protection Office. Over time, the camp got too big and visible. It showed Ireland’s problem with migration. Officials said that removing the tents was necessary because of problems with safety and hygiene . But some people say that it was a political thing. Ireland and the UK argued about migrants, and both governments had to do something. Some people thought moving the migrants was a good idea, but others said it was not fair. Authorities said that they moved them to help, but some people thought it was wrong. They believe that it is important to treat migrants with respect and find better ways to help them. Difficult words: refugee (a person who left their country to get away from war or other dangerous situations), hygiene (keeping yourself and things clean), treat (to behave towards someone or to deal with something in a particular way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

About 200 tents are in the center of Dublin. Migrants live there. The place is not safe anymore. It is dirty, too. Authorities decide to clear the tent city. Police use cars and trucks . Some people are happy that the tents are away. But other people believe this is about politics. The UK and Ireland fight about migrants. Both countries must do something. Clearing the tent city shows how big the problem is. Ireland must do something with migrants. But it is not easy. Ireland must find better ways to help them. Difficult words: tent (a shelter of strong cloth where people without home live), migrant (a person who moves to a place to have a better life), truck (a big car). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Apple CEO Tim Cook worries about the tech giant ’s future. There has been a significant drop in sales, the largest in over a year. Sales reached 90.8 billion dollars, which is a drop of 4% compared to the same period last year, primarily due to decreased demand for iPhones. Apple’s executives said the decline was caused by COVID-related supply disruptions, and they expect sales to rebound soon. They announced upcoming product launches and investments in AI. Although there have been problems such as increased competition and dropping sales in China, Apple is optimistic about its future. The company’s stock rose after announcing a share buyback and dividend increase. Difficult words: giant (an unusually big or powerful person or thing), rebound (to recover), dividend (a part of the profit of a company that is paid to the people who own shares in it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Apple boss Tim Cook talked about worries about the company’s future. Last year, Apple’s sales went down by 4% to 90.8 billion dollars. This happened mainly because fewer people wanted to buy iPhones. Leaders said that COVID-19 caused these problems. They think that sales will increase soon because of new products and AI. Although there are problems like more competition and fewer sales in China, Apple believes that things will get better again. People are happy about Apple’s plans, like new products and improvements in AI, which are very important for its future. Difficult words: sale (selling services and things), competition (a person or company who wants to be better than the others), improvement (making things better). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The company Apple has problems. People do not buy iPhones as much as in the past. Last year, Apple’s sales are 90.8 billion dollars. It is 4% less than the year before. Leaders say that this happens because of COVID-19. Companies do not have materials. They make fewer phones. Things are getting better now. Apple will have new products. They put a lot of money into AI . People are happy about Apple’s plans. They want new products. They like AI. These things are very important for Apple’s future . There are problems, like new companies in China. But Apple believes that things will work out well for them. Difficult words: sales (what a company sells), AI (artificial intelligence), future (time which will come). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
